Like, sometimes I'll catch myself just tapping the scanner in a little pattern, or I'll kind of freeze for a second with my hand hovering over the cash drawer while a customer is waiting. I felt terrible about it, because I always try to be a good employee. I just want to get it sorted out so I can do a good job. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking for?
Do these moments of getting stuck or doing these little patterns make you feel anxious or worried, or do they feel more like a habit you're just aware of?

Oh, um... no, I don't think they make me anxious. Not in the moment, anyway. It really is just... well, exactly like you said, kind of a little habit. I just sort of realize I'm doing it and think, 'Oh, silly me, better get back to work.' It doesn't scare me or anything like that. 

I mostly just... I just feel bad about it afterward because I don't want to inconvenience anyone, you know? I really pride myself on being polite and helpful at the store. So the only worry is just about letting my manager down or holding up a customer. I'm trying really hard to just be a good worker and fix it. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

When you find yourself doing those little patterns or freezing for a moment, is there a thought in your mind that makes you feel like you have to do it, or does it feel more like something you just end up doing without really thinking about it?

Well, um... no, not really. There isn't a specific thought behind it, like feeling I absolutely have to do it or anything like that. It's really just... exactly like your second point, something I just end up doing without thinking. 

My mind just sort of goes a little blank for a second, and my hand just does the tapping, or I just pause. I hope that doesn't make me sound too strange, or like I'm not paying attention to my job. I really do try my best to stay completely focused on the customers. I just sort of snap out of it and think, 'Whoops, back to work,' and move on. 

Did I explain that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
Before you find yourself tapping the scanner or pausing, do you ever feel a sort of urge or odd sensation that comes just before you do it?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I don't feel any kind of... odd sensation or an urge building up or anything like that. It's just, well, like I mentioned, it just sort of happens out of the blue. 

I hope that's not frustrating for you to hear, since I know you're trying to put the pieces together. I really wish I did feel something beforehand, honestly, because then maybe I could catch myself and stop it before my manager notices! But no, there's really no warning or urge at all. It's just a little blank spot. 

I hope that's an okay answer... am I giving you the kind of details you need? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
While you’re in the middle of one of these episodes—like tapping the scanner or pausing—do you feel completely aware of what’s going on around you, or does everything seem a bit fuzzy or distant?

Oh, um... no, I don't think it gets fuzzy or anything like that. I'm pretty sure I'm completely aware of everything going on. I can still hear the register beeping and the people talking in line, and the store music playing. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm completely checking out or ignoring my customers, because I really do try to stay alert. It's really just a brief little... physical pause, I guess you could say. But my ears and eyes are still working perfectly fine, and I'm right there the whole time. 

Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly for your notes. I hope I'm being helpful.

Can you remember everything that happens during one of these episodes afterward, like what the customer looked like or what they were buying, or do you ever feel confused about what just happened once it’s over?

Well, um... yes, I can usually remember everything just fine. I don't feel confused afterward, not really. I know exactly what the customer was buying, like if it was a gallon of milk or whatever. 

It's just... well, it's just that I keep getting stuck doing these little things that don't quite fit the moment, you know? Like I said, tapping the scanner in a pattern, or... or sometimes I'll just freeze with my hand hovering right over the open cash drawer while the poor customer is just standing there waiting. 

I really hate to admit this, because I pride myself on being a good worker, but... well, last week, it actually got me written up by my manager. I was so embarrassed. I really don't want you to think I'm a bad employee, I just... I get stuck for a second.
